text: Ich kann inzwischen besser mit Druck im Job umgehen. Ich arbeite in einer Agentur, und früher hat mich jede Deadline völlig aus der Bahn geworfen. Seit der Erfahrung nehme ich mir bewusst kleine Pausen, gehe mittags raus und sage auch mal, dass etwas nicht bis morgen geht. Ich bin nicht mehr ständig im Alarmmodus.
Better I think. Less anxious

I've been through a really stressful period since the experience: my partner was diagnosed with MS, I had to take on more work to cover our income, and my father went into a care home. Looking back, I'm amazed at how I coped. I think the experience gave me a deep sense that I can hold difficult things without collapsing. During the trip I went through waves of fear and grief that felt unbearable, and each time I let them wash over me, they passed. So when the diagnosis came, I let myself be scared and sad, and I didn't try to fix everything immediately. I also asked for help, which I never used to do. Friends brought food, my sister came for a week, and I joined a support group for partners of people with MS. I'm not saying it's been easy. There were nights when I cried in the bathroom so my partner wouldn't hear. But I never felt completely lost, and I've managed to stay present for her and for myself.
Ich sehe Probleme heute gelassener und weiß, dass sich vieles mit der Zeit von selbst regelt. Ich muss nicht sofort auf alles reagieren.
I'm more able to see when I'm overreacting and calm myself down before I say something I regret.

For me the experience was about recognising how much of my stress was self-created. I'm an academic, and I've spent my whole career in a state of low-grade panic: grant deadlines, reviewer comments, student evaluations, the constant feeling that I'm not publishing enough. During the experience I had this moment of seeing my life from the outside, and it was almost comical. All this suffering over things that, in the grand scheme, don't matter that much. I'm not saying my work doesn't matter, but my identity was completely fused with it, and every rejection felt like a judgement on my worth as a person. Since then I've been able to step back. When a paper gets rejected, I'm disappointed for a day and then I move on. I've stopped working on weekends. I also realised that a lot of my colleagues are in the same trap, and I've started talking about it openly, which has led to some surprisingly honest conversations in my department. My stress levels are much lower and, ironically, I think my work has gotten better.
Keine Veränderung, würde ich sagen.
I've learned to just let things be sometimes. I used to have to fix every problem right away, and now I can leave things for a while and come back to them when I'm calmer.

The main change is that I've become better at dealing with conflicts in my family. My parents are going through a messy divorce at the age of 60, and both of them want me on their side. Before the experience I would have been completely torn apart by this. Now I can listen to both of them without taking sides, and I can tell them when I need a break. I've also realised that their marriage problems are not my responsibility. That has been really freeing.

Ich habe das Gefühl, dass ich nach der Erfahrung zunächst sogar empfindlicher auf Stress reagiert habe. Ich war ein paar Monate lang sehr dünnhäutig. Inzwischen ist das vorbei, und ich würde sagen, ich gehe heute ungefähr so mit Stress um wie vorher, vielleicht etwas bewusster.

Honestly, the experience changed everything about how I handle stress. Before, I was the kind of person who would lie awake at night with my heart racing over things like an awkward conversation or a bill I forgot to pay. I had generalized anxiety disorder diagnosed at 19, and I'd been on and off medication for years. The experience was a guided session with psilocybin, and it was very intense. At one point I felt that my anxiety was a physical thing in my chest, like a clenched fist, and the guide asked me to breathe into it. Slowly it opened up, and what was underneath was just tenderness, like a sore spot. I cried for a long time. Since then, when I feel anxious, I do the same thing: I find where it sits in my body and I breathe into it. It doesn't always make the anxiety go away, but it changes my relationship to it. I'm not fighting it anymore. I've had some big stressful events since, including a car accident and a job change, and I coped much better than I would have before.
It's easier to stay calm, I don't get flustered so quickly

Ich versuche, belastende Situationen aus einer gewissen Distanz zu betrachten, als würde ich mir selbst von außen zuschauen. Das habe ich in der Erfahrung gelernt, als ich eine Zeit lang das Gefühl hatte, über mir zu schweben und mich selbst zu beobachten. Das hilft mir, nicht so tief in meine Gefühle zu rutschen.

I've started to treat myself the way I'd treat a friend going through a hard time. When something stressful happens, I used to beat myself up: why did I let this happen, I'm so stupid, I should have known. Now I try to be kind. I say things to myself like, this is really hard, it makes sense that you're upset. It sounds cheesy but it makes a huge difference in how quickly I bounce back. I think the experience showed me how harsh my inner voice was.
I can't really say. I'm still the same stressed person I always was.

Durch die Erfahrung habe ich mehr Vertrauen in mich selbst gewonnen. Wenn etwas Schwieriges passiert, denke ich nicht mehr gleich, dass ich das nicht schaffe. Ich habe gesehen, dass ich viel mehr aushalten kann, als ich dachte.

The way I handle stress is completely different now, and I think it comes down to one thing: I'm no longer trying to escape from myself. Before the experience I was always running, from my feelings, from my past, from silence. I filled every moment with work, podcasts, social media, drinks with friends. When something stressful happened, I'd just run faster. During the experience I couldn't run anymore. I had to sit with everything, and it was terrifying at first, but then it became peaceful. I realised that underneath all the running there was a deep loneliness and a feeling that I'm not enough. Once I saw that, I couldn't unsee it. Now I try to stop and feel when I'm stressed instead of running. I go for walks without headphones. I sit with a cup of tea and just notice what's happening inside. I've also cut back on drinking. It's harder in some ways because I feel more, but I'm much more stable. I don't get the big crashes I used to get after months of running on empty.
I'm better at accepting help from others when I'm stressed.

Ich habe gemerkt, dass ich in stressigen Zeiten oft unfair zu meinem Partner werde, weil ich meinen Frust an ihm auslasse. Seit der Erfahrung achte ich mehr darauf und entschuldige mich, wenn es doch passiert. Wir reden mehr darüber, was uns belastet.

The experience gave me a kind of inner compass. I'm a doctor and my job is incredibly stressful, especially since the pandemic. I've seen colleagues burn out and leave medicine. During the experience I reconnected with why I chose this profession: I care about people and I want to help them. That sounds obvious, but I had completely lost touch with it under the pressure of numbers and shifts. Now, when a shift is overwhelming, I try to focus on the one patient in front of me. It grounds me. I've also reduced my hours to 80 percent, which my department wasn't thrilled about.
It made me realize I can survive almost anything
Ich bin in stressigen Situationen heute klarer im Kopf. Früher war ich dann wie gelähmt, heute kann ich überlegen, was zu tun ist, und Schritt für Schritt vorgehen.

Since the experience I've been better at dealing with my anger. I still get angry when things go wrong, but I can feel it in my body before it explodes, and I can take a step back. My kids noticed it too.

Die Erfahrung hat meinen Umgang mit belastenden Lebensereignissen grundlegend verändert. Ich hatte eine sehr schwierige Kindheit mit einem gewalttätigen Vater und habe gelernt, bei Stress sofort in eine Art Erstarrung zu verfallen. Ich war dann wie abgeschaltet, konnte nicht mehr denken und nicht mehr fühlen. In der Erfahrung habe ich diese Erstarrung sehr deutlich gespürt, und dann habe ich erlebt, wie sie sich langsam gelöst hat. Mein Körper hat gezittert, ich habe geweint, und danach war ich erschöpft, aber leicht. Seitdem merke ich, wenn ich wieder in die Erstarrung gehe, und kann mich manchmal da rausholen, indem ich mich bewege, schüttle oder bewusst atme. Ich mache außerdem eine Traumatherapie, in der ich das weiter bearbeite. Bei den letzten größeren Belastungen, einer Kündigung und einem Streit mit meiner Schwester, bin ich viel handlungsfähiger geblieben als früher.
Ich gehe jetzt regelmäßig zum Yoga, das hilft mir sehr bei Stress.

I think I'm much less of a perfectionist now, and that has reduced the stress in my life a lot. Not everything has to be done perfectly, and it's okay to make mistakes. I've also learned to delegate at work.

I deal with stressful events by reminding myself of the bigger picture. During the experience I had a vision of my life as a long river, with rapids and calm stretches, and I understood that the rapids are part of the journey. When I'm in a rough patch now, I tell myself I'm in the rapids and that calmer water will come. It has helped me through a redundancy, my mother's death and a breakup. Each time I was sad and scared, but I didn't lose hope.
Ich bin weniger ängstlich, wenn etwas Unvorhergesehenes passiert, und kann flexibler reagieren. Mein Leben ist dadurch entspannter geworden.
I'm more grounded and less likely to get swept up in other people's drama or panic. I'm the calm one in my friend group now.

For a long time I dealt with stress by shutting down emotionally. I'd go numb, keep functioning, and not feel anything until much later, when I'd collapse into depression. During the experience the numbness lifted completely, and I felt everything I had been storing up: grief over my brother's suicide, anger at my parents, fear about my future. It was overwhelming, but I had a very good sitter who stayed with me. Since then, I've been learning to stay in contact with my feelings when stressful things happen. It's not easy, because the numbness is a deep habit. But I notice it now, and I can sometimes choose to let the feelings in. I've also started writing, which helps me process what's happening. When my company went bankrupt earlier this year, I felt the fear and anger in real time, talked to my partner about it, and didn't fall into a depression afterwards, which has happened every other time. That felt like a real victory.
Ich denke, ich bin geduldiger geworden.

I've learned that most of my stress comes from future thinking. I'm always worried about what might happen. The experience brought me into the present so completely that I saw how much of my life I'd been missing. Now when I'm stressed I try to come back to now.

Since the experience I have a different relationship with failure, which used to be the source of most of my stress. I failed my driving test three times before the experience and each time I was devastated for weeks. After the experience I failed it once more, and I laughed about it and booked the next one. Passed on the fifth try. That's a small example, but it shows how differently I see setbacks. I don't take them as proof that I'm useless anymore.

Seitdem ich die Erfahrung gemacht habe, reagiere ich auf Stress deutlich ruhiger. Ich weiß, dass ich nicht sofort handeln muss, und kann mir Zeit nehmen, nachzudenken. Auch bei Konflikten bleibe ich gelassener und kann zuhören, statt mich zu verteidigen.
I'm about the same as before, maybe a tiny bit calmer.

The experience taught me how to surrender, which has been the most important skill for handling stress. I used to be a control freak, I planned everything and if things didn't go to plan I'd have a meltdown. During the experience I fought the effects for the first hour, trying to stay in control, and it got worse and worse until I was in full panic. Then my sitter told me to stop fighting and let go, and when I finally did, it was like stepping out of a storm into sunshine. I've thought about that moment almost every day since. When something stressful happens now, I try to notice where I'm fighting reality, and I let go a little. Not completely, I still plan and I still care, but I don't grip so tightly. It's made me much calmer and more flexible. My wedding last summer was a disaster weather-wise, it poured all day, and I just laughed and danced in the rain.
Ich habe eher das Gefühl, dass ich seither schneller gestresst bin. Ich bin empfindlicher geworden und brauche mehr Ruhe.

I've learned to set healthy boundaries, which has reduced the number of stressful situations in my life. I used to say yes to everything and then feel resentful and overwhelmed. During the experience I saw how I abandon myself to please others. Since then I've been practising saying no. It was scary at first, I thought people would be angry, but most of them just accepted it. My stress levels have gone way down.
I don't really feel stressed anymore, I just deal with it

Ich bin achtsamer geworden und merke schneller, wenn mich etwas belastet. Dann versuche ich, gut für mich zu sorgen, z.B. mit Bewegung, Schlaf oder einem Gespräch mit einer Freundin. Das klappt meistens ganz gut.
